name: 15-sbml-adaptive-coevolution
title: SBML-driven adaptive coevolution (proposed)
question: When the continuous node state (an SBML readout) itself drives the rewiring, does a self-organised modular topology emerge?
hypothesis: Letting each node rewire toward neighbours with a similar SBML observable (e.g. oscillator phase) closes the state→topology feedback and self-organises the network into phase-coherent modules.
objective: Couple an SBML-observable-driven rewiring rule to the Family-B reactors, so topology and continuous state co-adapt (the continuous generalisation of study 07).
description:
Proposed follow-up seeded from study 07. The continuous-state analogue of adaptive coevolution: the richest point in the OF↔ON feedback loop.

(Baseline points at the composite this proposal would EXTEND; the new mechanism is not yet built.)

expected_behavior.name: state-driven-modules
expected_behavior.condition: phase-coherent modules emerge from state-driven rewiring
expected_behavior.rationale: Adaptive rewiring toward like-state neighbours is known to fragment networks into assortative communities (Gross & Blasius).

report.verdict_detail: Proposed follow-up — not yet built or run. Seeded from 07-adaptive-coevolution (sbml-on-adaptive).
